reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Thursday at the end of July. Nothing about today announces itself. No milestone, no crisis, no anniversary — just a regular weekday in the middle of summer. And that's exactly the point. When I was drinking, I couldn't stand ordinary Thursdays. They felt like something to escape from, or drink through, or at least reward myself for surviving. The whole week was scaffolding for the weekend, and the weekend was scaffolding for oblivion.

What sobriety quietly hands you, if you stay long enough to notice, is Thursday. Just Thursday. Coffee that tastes like coffee. A workout you actually remember. A conversation with someone that isn't performed through a filter of what you drank last night or what you'll drink tonight. The ordinary stops being the enemy and starts being the material. Durant's line about Aristotle gets at this: the life you're building isn't built in the big dramatic moments. It's built in what you repeatedly do on days that don't matter.

Eleven years in, I can tell you the good life isn't a highlight reel. It's a stack of unremarkable days you were actually present for. Ski trips and skydives and hunting seasons are real, and they're better sober — but they rest on the foundation of a hundred quiet Thursdays where you showed up, did the next right thing, and went to bed clear-headed. Today is one of those days. Don't waste it waiting for something else.
reflection.meditation: Where in today can I be fully present instead of waiting for it to be over?

affirmations: I am building my life in the small hours, not the big moments.
Today I don't need to escape my own Thursday.
I am someone who shows up — for the ordinary and the extraordinary alike.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a day that asks nothing dramatic of me. Grateful for a clear head at 7am, for work I can actually do, for people who know the real version of me. Grateful that I don't have to manage a hangover, a lie, or a version of myself I can't stand. The bar is on the floor and I'm still amazed I get to walk over it sober.
gratitude.closing: One ordinary Thursday at a time.
